content.text: I want to make some comprehensive improvements to the audio handling in our tool. I've added a sample audio file 'samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a', which was recorded with my RODE USB desktop mic. I want to be able to turn that into usable audio for videos. The first issue is "Normalize", which simple bumped the volume level up to the max of 400%. That is still below what would be the max. This audio sample is pretty clean, so it could be increased even more without issue. 400% should not be a hard max.
I'll start by looking at how Normalize and the gain cap work today, and at the sample.

# The same five, under the round-to-NEAREST the cap used to get: the
    # measured peak is the report's own true peak less its gain, so this is
    # arithmetic over what the app just answered rather than a second guess.
    nearest = [
        ceiling for ceiling, r in zip(ceilings, reports)
        if round((ceiling - (r["true_peak_dbtp"] - r["gain_db"])) / 0.01) * 0.01
        > (ceiling - (r["true_peak_dbtp"] - r["gain_db"])) + 1e-12
    ]
    check(
        len(nearest) >= 1,
        f"…and the sweep is not vacuous: {len(nearest)} of the five would have landed "
        f"over the ceiling had the cap been rounded to the NEAREST hundredth "
        f"({[f'{x:g}' for x in nearest]})",
    )

    # A mix past full scale. The measure pass reads 32-bit float, and since
    # #86 so does the write pass of a NORMALISED export: the gain is applied
    # to the float mix and quantised once, so the file is the measured signal
    # turned down, unclipped. Only the same mix written with NO gain goes
    # through the 16-bit decode, which saturates, and that report must say so.
    print("\n5d — a mix past full scale: gained in float, clipped only without a gain")
    o = Session(mcp, "phase5-overscale")
    hot_clip = o.place("half.wav")
    # A half-scale tone at the model's 4× ceiling: +6 dBFS of mix, which is
    # what two normalised clips on two tracks would also give.
    o.op("set_audio", clips=[hot_clip], patch={"volume": 4})
    _, hot, hot_result = o.wav("hot", loudness_lufs=-14, peak_dbtp=-1)
    report = hot_result["loudness"]
    mix_peak = report["sample_peak_dbfs"] - report["gain_db"]
    check(
        mix_peak > 1.0,
        f"the mix really did pass full scale, or nothing below is a check — the measure "
        f"pass reads float and saw {fmt(mix_peak)} dBFS before the gain",
    )
    check(
        "clipped" not in report["summary"],
        f"the normalised export does NOT say the mix clipped: it was gained in float "
        f"before it was quantised ({report['summary']})",
    )
    written = integrated(channels(hot))
    check(
        written is not None and abs(written - report["integrated_lufs"]) <= 0.5,
        f"the file this script decoded measures {fmt(written)} LUFS against the "
        f"{fmt(report['integrated_lufs'])} reported — within ±0.5 LU, so the figure is "
        f"the file's",
    )
    full = sum(1 for s in samples(hot) if s in (-32768, 32767))
    check(
        full == 0,
        f"and no decoded sample sits at full scale ({full} at −32768 or 32767)",
    )
    _, raw, raw_result = o.wav("hot-plain")
    raw_full = sum(1 for s in samples(raw) if s in (-32768, 32767))
    check(
        "clipped" in raw_result["loudness"]["summary"] and raw_full > 0,
        f"but the same mix exported WITHOUT a gain is clipped by the 16-bit decode and "
            'bad value at "volume" in an audio patch: expected a number, not "loud"',
            clips=[clip], patch={"volume": "loud"})
    refused(s, "set_audio", "an unknown key spelled with a null",
            'unknown key "pann" in an audio patch',
            clips=[clip], patch={"pann": None})
    # The range refusals are `props_check.rs`'s and carry the GROUP's name

    refused(s, "set_audio", "a volume past the ceiling",

"""Road map 2, phase 5 — Sound, driven against the built binary over MCP.

Every claim here is one of two things: a SAMPLE-FOR-SAMPLE comparison of two
decoded exports, or a number this script measured off an exported file with
its own arithmetic. Nothing is believed because the app reported it — the
whole point of 5d is that an export can report −14.0 LUFS and write something
else, and a check that reads the report back is a check that build would
pass.

The five parts, and what each is measured with:

* **5a the mono fold** — three claims off one fixture whose channels are
  DIFFERENT (440 Hz at half scale left, 880 Hz at a quarter right), because
  "left equals right" is a tautology on any of the stereo tones in `media/`.
  With `mono` on the two channels are equal sample for sample; each of those
  samples is within one 16-bit LSB of the MEAN of the two channels the same
  timeline writes with `mono` off, which is what tells an average from
  "copy the left channel over the right"; and setting `mono` and clearing it
  again writes a file byte-identical to the one written before it was ever
  set. That last is the baseline the contract's D-A5 asks for, taken HERE
  rather than read off a stored file: a pre-phase binary is not available to
  a script, and a stored one would only prove that a file on disk had not
  changed.

  The same three claims are then made of a NEST clip's `mono`, over a clip
  panned hard left BEFORE it was nested — the one arrangement that tells a
  fold of the nest's MIX from a fold carried down to the head of the inner
  clip's own chain, which would run before that pan and leave the file hard
  left. A nest clip's id names no audio segment, so this is the case where
  the checkbox was accepted, kept lit and saved while folding nothing.

* **5b the meters** — NOT PROVED HERE, and this is the honest statement of
  why. `LevelMeter` publishes a struct to a view (`LevelMeterView`) and
  nothing in `AgentCatalog.swift` reaches it: the meter's model has no MCP
  surface at all, so there is no call this script could make that would read
  a level off it, and adding a tool so that a proof could exist would be the
  proof deciding the product's API. The contract's own claim — that a
  −20 dBFS tone publishes −20 dBFS within ±0.5 dB — is a unit-style check
  against `LevelMeter`, and the resting appearance D-B5 fixes is what
  `phase5_chrome.py` photographs offscreen. Neither belongs in a script whose
  currency is exports and rendered frames.

* **5c Normalise Clip** — the placement is read back through the tool, and
  then the LEVEL is measured on an exported WAV. A −6 dBFS tone normalises to
  a file whose loudest sample is −1 dBFS ±0.1; a −40 dBFS tone cannot get
  there (the model's volume ceiling is 4×) and its file lands at the −27.96
  the result claimed rather than at −1, which is the whole of D-C7. The
  refusals are read for the words that name the clip: a silent clip, a clip
  whose peaks file this script DELETED off the package (the deterministic
  spelling of "not analysed yet"), a clip id that is not in the project, and a
  NEST — whose sound is measured coming out of the export first, because the
  claim about that refusal is that it does not tell a clip you can hear that it
  plays no sound.
  One job's failure is one job's problem — a mixed call normalises the good
  clip and reports the other under `skipped`. And the reversed mirror is
  measured by the only means that can tell it from its absence: a fixture
  loud in its first half and quiet in its second, trimmed to its first 1.4 s
  forwards and backwards, must measure 20 dB apart.

* **5d loudness on export** — the script implements BS.1770-4 (below) and

#
# One `aevalsrc` expression per channel, so the amplitude and the phase of
# every fixture are written here and are exact. All are 48 kHz 16-bit stereo
# WAV, which is what the export mix is, so nothing is resampled anywhere.

FIXTURE_EXPRESSIONS = {
    # 5a. The channels must DIFFER or "left equals right" proves nothing:
    # 440 Hz at −6.02 dBFS left, 880 Hz at −12.04 dBFS right. The mono fold's
    # answer, max over t of |0.5·sin(a) + 0.25·sin(2a)|/2, is about −9.8 dBFS
    # — a number neither channel holds, which is why the mean can be asserted.
    "lr.wav": ("0.5*sin(2*PI*440*t)", "0.25*sin(2*PI*880*t)", 2),
    # 5c and 5d. A plain tone at exactly half scale: −6.020600 dBFS, which

    "half.wav": ("0.5*sin(2*PI*440*t)", "0.5*sin(2*PI*440*t)", 3),

    # 5c's reversed mirror: loud for 1.5 s, then 20 dB down for 1.5 s.
    "ramp.wav": (

    "fs4.wav": (

"""Issue batch B70 (#220) — the spec indexes' Lines cells against `wc -l`,

`designs/spec/README.md` and `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md` each carry

cell is that file's line count (the number of newline bytes, what `wc -l`
prints). The FOLDER row (`11-decisions/`, linking its README) reads
`<N> in <M> files`: N is the summed line count of every `*.md` in the folder,

every `*.md` in `designs/spec/` but the README has exactly one row there,
every subdirectory has a folder row, and every `*.md` in `11-decisions/` but

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The owner's pass over a clip's sound, begun 2026-10-30 to turn a desktop USB microphone's
recording into usable audio for a video. Its IDs are the AU- series. Each was recorded before
its code.

- **AU-1 — `audio.volume`'s ceiling is ×32 (+30.1 dB), not ×4; the Volume slider keeps its
  0–400 % travel and the field beside it takes the rest (owner, 2026-10-30: "400% should not be
  a hard max").** The owner's recording `Rode-usb-mic.m4a` (a RØDE USB desktop microphone,
  30.4 s of AAC mono at 48 kHz) peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated loudness of −44.7 LUFS
  (ffmpeg's `volumedetect` and `ebur128`), so Normalize wanted ×7.55 to reach −1 dBFS and stopped
  at ×4, −6.5 dBFS. The ceiling stays — `MAX_GAIN` still bounds `check_audio`'s refusal,
  `clamp_audio` and the envelope, so one bad patch cannot send +80 dB to the mix — but at ×32:
  Normalize now reaches −1 dBFS from a peak as quiet as −31.1 dBFS, and 30 dB covers the gap
  between this microphone's −44.7 LUFS and a −14 LUFS delivery. 32 rather than 31.62 (exactly
  +30 dB) so the refusal reads a whole number: "audio.volume must be between 0 and 32".
  - Measured before the change: AVFoundation's audio mix applies a `setVolumeRamp` volume above
    4 exactly. The recording read through `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput` in 32-bit float peaks at
    4.000, 7.600, 16.000, 32.000 and 64.000 times its ×1 peak at those volumes (a scratch probe
    of 2026-10-30), so ×4 was the model's rule and nothing beneath it changes.
  - The Volume row: the slider keeps 0–400 %, where its resolution is useful (a 0–3200 % rail
    would put 100 % at a thirty-second of its width); the field takes 0–3200 %. A value above
    400 % pins the knob at the rail's end, and a drag writes the rail's own range. The quick
    picks are unchanged.
  - One Swift copy of the ceiling, `AudioNormalize.maxGain`, which the Volume row's field and
    the agent's sentences now read too, is held to the core's refusal by `core/tests/audio_gain.rs`,
    reading its `static let` line as `graphic_ffi.rs` reads `maxTextureSide`. No `rc_*` export:
    `ReelCore.swift` is over its cap, and one constant does not need the FFI.

    (`Project::validate` does not call `check_audio`), so an older build opens a project with a
    volume above 4, plays it at ×4 through `audio.rs`'s clamp and writes the stored number back
    unchanged. A bump guards against a loss on that round trip, and there is none.
  - What it accepts: a mix can go further past full scale than before. The preview's output and
    an un-normalised export clip there (phase 5d's 16-bit decode, which says so); a normalised
    export gains in float (#86) and does not. Normalize itself still lands at −1 dBFS.

def peak_dbfs(file):
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["ffmpeg", "-hide_banner", "-nostats", "-i", file, "-af", "volumedetect",
         "-f", "null", "-"], capture_output=True, text=True).stderr
    return float(out.split("max_volume:")[1].split("dB")[0])


media = mcp.call("import_media", project=path, path=sample)["media"]

track = mcp.call("get_project", project=path)["project"]["tracks"][0]["id"]
clip = mcp.call("add_clip", project=path, track=track, media=media, at=0)["new_clips"][0]

content.text:
Normalize is no longer capped at 400 %. The volume ceiling is now 3200 % (×32, about +30 dB), and your RØDE recording normalizes cleanly. The gate passes, and the two proofs I changed pass on the Release build; nothing is committed.

**Your sample:** it peaks at −18.6 dBFS, so Normalize now sets the volume to 755 % (+17.6 dB), and the exported WAV peaks at −1.0 dBFS. The old cap stopped it at 400 %, peaking at −6.5 dBFS.

**What changed**
- **The ceiling:** the 4× limit was only a rule in the Rust core. I checked that AVFoundation's mix applies the gain exactly at 7.6×, 16×, 32× and 64×, then raised the core's limit to 32. A limit is still there so one bad edit can't send +80 dB to the mix. Normalize now reaches −1 dBFS for anything whose peak is above about −31 dBFS.
- **Volume control:**
  - The slider still covers 0–400 %, because a 0–3200 % slider would squeeze 100 % into the first thirty-second of its travel.
  - The number field beside it accepts up to 3200 %.
  - Above 400 % the knob sits at the right end while the field shows the real value.
  - I checked this in the running app: it reads 755 %, +17.6 dB.
- **Keeping the two copies in step:** the Swift side has one copy of the limit, which Normalize, the field and the agent's tool descriptions all read. A new core test, `core/tests/audio_gain.rs`, fails if that copy and the core's limit disagree. I confirmed it fails when either one is changed.
- **Older builds:** no project format change was needed. An older build opens a project with a volume above 400 %, plays it at 400 %, and saves the value back unchanged.
- **Records:**
  - The decision is AU-1 in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md`, a new file for this audio pass.
  - The spec text, the user guide (`docs/guide/audio.md`) and two existing tests that used 9 as an out-of-range volume are updated.
  - Phase 5's proof gains a case for a quiet −20 dBFS source.
  - `docs/manual-checks.md` gains SE-22: listen to the louder playback in the preview, which no script can check.

**Still to come:** −1 dBFS peak isn't delivery loudness yet. Your recording measures −44.7 LUFS, so after Normalize it's around −27 LUFS, well below the usual −14 to −16 for video. Closing that gap needs a compressor or limiter plus loudness targeting, which is likely your next issue.

**Decision for you:** `samples/` is untracked in the worktree. Should I commit your recording or add it to `.gitignore`?
Commit it. We should make other useful samples as well and add them later.

# 1. What this is

A screencast editor without a recorder — and, since road map 3,
a recorder of the SCREEN, and since §11 CAM-1 of a camera beside it or on its
own, whose output is ordinary media. Open one or
more video files from disk, arrange them on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, trim,
split, annotate, animate, and export. Mac only, Apple Silicon, macOS 26+.

The bar is a balance: enough to make a real cut with text,
shapes, transitions and simple animation, without Final Cut's magnetic
timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin ecosystem.

Deliberate non-goals: multicam, color grading beyond
per-clip controls (§11 GR-1: tier 1 of grading — tone, adjustment clips,
looks, LUT import, an ungraded switch and one luma waveform — is in, kept by
the owner's verdict of 2026-10-10, and tier 2's scopes, colour wheels,
curves and qualifiers beside it, GR-10…GR-13; tier 3's HDR→SDR conversion
and camera log are in, GR-15, GR-16; the HDR road map's HLG timeline, its
HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables, HDR scopes, the PQ peak, Canon Log
2 and 3 and opt-in linear-light blending are in, HD-1…HD-17; a wide-gamut
working space for SDR projects is not wanted, GR-20; tier 4's vectorscope zoom,
hue curves, the blend between curves of different point counts and the
qualifier's cleanup blur are in, GR-24, GR-31…GR-35, while an Offset
wheel, a qualifier on picture clips, 1,024-level scopes and a histogram
behind the curves are not wanted, GR-27…GR-30), audio beyond what shipped
(volume, fades, duck, pan, compressor, noise reduction, peak normalize, the
transition crossfade and the export's loudness target — M3 and §11 R5-2; so
no EQ, mix buses or Audio Units, while offline voice effects are deferred
rather than out), a plugin system (a clip may draw itself from a JavaScript
module in its package, road map 10; nothing else is scriptable — §11 G-1),
motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe (heavy
pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape — road map 2 §4),
any platform but macOS. **Screen recording was on this list until road map 3
reversed it** (§11): the app records a display or a window through
ScreenCaptureKit into a file it then imports exactly as File ▸ Open would —
paused and resumed from the menu bar, each stretch its own file and its own
clip; callouts reconstructed after the fact stay out. **Camera recording
was on it too until §11 CAM-1** (road map "camera-recording") reversed it: a
camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and clip.

**The opening flow is the point.** File > Open on a `.mov` or `.mp4` (or a
drop on the Dock icon, or the welcome window's Open Video…) creates an
*untitled* project sized to that file, with the file as the first clip on
Track 1, ready to cut. Save then writes a `.framejob` package next to the
source. The app is also the Alternate handler for movie, audio and image
types so Open With… works from the Finder.

input.prompt:
You are researching for Frame Job, a macOS video editor (Swift/AppKit over a Rust core) in the git worktree /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/audio-updates. Work ONLY inside that directory. The owner asked: "Review the audio editing features of other video editing tools. What other audio editing features should we support to be considered a professional-grade tool?"

## Your deliverable
Write ONE Markdown file: `designs/audio-survey.md` (the repo keeps an open survey in `designs/` — see `designs/adr/effects-survey.md` for the house shape: a Status line, context, findings, proposals). Write nothing else: no code, no other docs, no commits, no GitHub issues. When done, reply with a short summary: the top gaps in priority order, and anything you could not verify.

## Method — primary sources only
Every claim about another editor must cite the vendor's own documentation (official user guide/manual/help page/release notes), with its URL. Do not cite blogs, YouTube or review sites as evidence; if a first-party source can't be found, mark the claim "unverified" rather than dropping or asserting it. Use WebSearch (mode "standard" by default; "extended" only when standard results are thin) and WebFetch. Batch independent searches in one turn. Primary sources to start from:
- DaVinci Resolve (Fairlight page, Edit page audio, Fairlight FX, Voice Isolation, Dialogue Leveler, Ducker, Loudness/metering, bus routing, ADR, automation) — Blackmagic's DaVinci Resolve Reference Manual / "What's new" pages.
- Final Cut Pro — Apple's Final Cut Pro User Guide (support.apple.com/guide/final-cut-pro): audio enhancements (Voice Isolation, Loudness, Noise Removal, Hum Removal, EQ/Match Audio), roles and audio lanes, audio components / channel configuration, keyframes, Logic effects, Audio Units, meters, fades, expanding audio for J/L cuts.
- Premiere Pro — Adobe helpx: Essential Sound panel, Enhance Speech, Auto Ducking, Remix, Loudness auto-match, Audio Track Mixer / submixes, Audio Clip Mixer, keyframes / rubber bands, Loudness Radar, effects (DeNoise, DeReverb, Parametric EQ, Hard Limiter, DeEsser), Audition round-trip.
- Creator tier: Descript (Studio Sound, Edit for Clarity, ducking, loudness), CapCut desktop (voice enhancement, noise reduction, voice changer, beat detection), Camtasia (TechSmith: audio effects, noise removal, emphasize/ducking, volume leveling), ScreenFlow (Telestream: audio filters, ducking, normalization, smoothing).
Also cite Apple developer docs for which built-in Audio Units / AVFoundation pieces could implement a gap on macOS (e.g. AUNBandEQ, AUDynamicsProcessor, AUPeakLimiter, AUMultibandCompressor, AUReverb2, AVAudioUnitEQ, voice processing / voice isolation APIs, Sound Analysis). Feasibility notes are secondary — keep them to one line each.

## What Frame Job already has (read these, they are written from the code)
- `docs/guide/audio.md` — the whole audio feature set: volume (now to 3200 %, spec §11 AU-1), mute, Normalize (peak), fades, ducking by clip extent, mono, pan, Keep pitch, compressor ("Smooth volume levels"), noise reduction (steady noise only), track mute/solo, level meter, Synchronize Audio, Detach Audio, volume actions (keyframe-like animation on an action lane), crossfades on transitions.
- `docs/guide/export.md` — export loudness target (LUFS, true-peak ceiling), audio-only formats.
- `docs/guide/cleanup-tools.md` — Remove Silences (on-device VAD), Remove Filler Words (AssemblyAI, bring-your-own key).
- `docs/guide/speed.md`, `docs/guide/captions.md`, `docs/guide/screen-recording.md` (microphone recording, voice-over) — skim for audio-relevant parts.
- `designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md` — scope. IMPORTANT: it currently lists as deliberate non-goals "audio beyond what shipped ... so no EQ, mix buses or Audio Units, while offline voice effects are deferred rather than out", and also multicam, roles, a plugin ecosystem. The owner has reversed non-goals before (colour grading, screen and camera recording) when asked. So: recommend what a professional tool needs regardless, but FLAG each recommendation that would require the owner to lift a current non-goal, naming which one.
Read the guide pages before writing the gap list so nothing is reported missing that exists.

## Context for priorities
The owner's immediate goal is turning a quiet but clean RØDE USB desktop-mic voice recording (`samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`: peak −18.6 dBFS, integrated −44.7 LUFS, LRA 21.1 LU) into usable audio for videos, as part of a "comprehensive audio improvements" pass. Frame Job is a screencast/creator-oriented editor that wants to be professional-grade. Constraints: macOS 26+, Apple Silicon only; AVFoundation, no ffmpeg in the product; the project is open source and every cloud AI feature is bring-your-own-key (no hosted relay). On-device features are preferred.

## Structure of the file
1. Status (Survey, 2026-10-30; proposals only — nothing here is a spec §11 decision) and the question.
2. Frame Job today — a compact inventory (cite the guide pages).
3. Per-editor findings — what each editor offers in audio, grouped (cleanup/repair, dynamics & loudness, EQ & tone, mixing & routing, automation/keyframing, editing workflow such as J/L cuts and audio-only trims, metering & analysis, sync & multitrack, AI/voice, delivery & stems, effects & plugins), each item cited.
4. A feature matrix: rows = features, columns = Resolve, FCP, Premiere, Descript, CapCut, Camtasia, ScreenFlow, Frame Job (yes / partial / no, with a footnote where partial).
5. The gap list, tiered: (A) needed to be called professional-grade, (B) expected by the creator/screencast audience, (C) nice to have. For each: what it is, who has it (cited), why it matters for Frame Job's users, a one-line Apple-framework feasibility note, and "lifts non-goal: …" where applicable. Call out explicitly which gaps a quiet desktop-mic voice recording needs first (e.g. loudness-targeted normalization per clip, limiter, EQ/high-pass, de-ess, voice isolation, dialogue leveling — verify, don't assume).
6. Useful sample recordings to add to `samples/` (the owner wants more real samples): a short list of recordings, each tied to the gaps it would exercise (e.g. a voice with HVAC hum, a sibilant voice, a clipped/too-hot take, a reverberant room on a laptop mic, a two-person interview, a music bed under speech).
7. Sources — every URL cited.

## House rules for the file
- Never write the product's old name (it was renamed to Frame Job; a check fails on the old spelling).
- Plain, direct prose; tables where they help. No length budget, but keep it readable — favour precise tables and short cited bullets over essays.
- Use typographic minus (−) for negative levels, as the repo does.

# 2. The six ideas, and why the model stays simple

Six ideas do most of the work. Frame Job is built on all six.

1. **One kind of track.** Every track holds any clip — video, audio,
   still, text, shape. There are no video-vs-audio track types; an
   audio-only clip simply draws a waveform. Higher track = in front.
2. **A fixed canvas with direct manipulation.** The document has a size
   (1920×1080 by default). Clips are placed on it by dragging on the
   preview; scale, position, rotation and crop are clip properties with
   numbers in the inspector and handles on the canvas.
3. **Actions, not keyframes.** An Action is a span on a clip with an
   easing curve. You edit the property values at the *end* of the span;
   the values at the start are whatever was already in effect. There is
   no keyframe graph.
4. **Overlap is a transition.** Sliding one clip over its neighbour on
   the same track makes a transition of that length. No transition
   track, no browser to drag from.
5. **One inspector, tabbed by what the selection is.** Video / Audio /
   Text / Shape for the selected clip; Media and Document always.
6. **A small keyboard vocabulary.** ⌘T split, W/E trim to playhead,
   ⌘⌫ ripple delete, ⇧⌘F freeze frame, M marker, Space/JKL transport.

Left out: everything that only makes sense for a recording
it made itself (mouse/keyboard/touch callouts, pointer effects), templates,
publishing to YouTube/Vimeo, the stock-media library.
----
# Spec §11 — decisions: Foundations (M1–M3, road map 2)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

- **AVFoundation, not ffmpeg.** Risk: MKV, WebM/VP9 and AV1-in-MKV do not
  open. Mitigation (M3, landed): an opt-in import step that shells out to a
  user-installed ffmpeg (present at `/opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg` on the
  development machine) to rewrap or transcode. The conversion is written to
  `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, **not into the
  package**, for two reasons the `FFmpegRewrap.rewrapDirectory` comment
  spells out: opening an MKV from the Finder makes an UNTITLED document, so
  the import that needs a conversion is exactly the one with no package to
  put it in; and `fileWrapper(ofType:)` is a two-child whitelist whose one
  surviving location, `cache/`, is documented-regenerable (§5.6) — the last
  place for the only decodable copy of someone's footage. The name carries
  a digest of path, size and modification date, so a conversion is reused
  and invalidates itself. `RCFFmpegImport` chooses the policy and
  `RCFFmpegPath` the binary; with neither ffmpeg nor a cached conversion
  the import fails exactly as it did before the feature existed.
  Amended by #216-R: WebM and Matroska open by a built-in rewrap; ffmpeg
  remains the opt-in step for what that does not copy.
  Amended by #227: that step copies a constant-rate VP9 Profile 0 or 2
  video stream rather than re-encoding it, kept only when every frame of
  the copy is on its rate's grid.
  **Amended by NM-4** (rename R0):
  `~/Library/Application Support/Reelcut/Rewrapped/` is now
  `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`.
- **Custom compositor from day one** (M1 step 5). `AVVideoCompositing`
  has sharp edges — pixel-buffer pools, timing, `renderContextChanged`.
  Building the single-layer version first de-risks every later effect.
- **`AVPlayerLayer` under an overlay view**, not a self-driven `MTKView`,
  for the preview: A/V sync and scrubbing come from the player; the
  overlay maps through `videoRect`.
- **One JSON op entry point** (`rc_project_apply`) instead of one C
  function per op. Trade-off accepted: argument checking moves to
  Rust (`Err`) and to the typed Swift builders; in return the header is
  stable and the MCP catalog is the same table.
- **The plan-string compare** decides rebuild vs. refresh. Simple, and
  correct by construction because the plan contains exactly the

Spec scope limits sit in three places: `01-what-this-is.md` (the non-goals), `02-six-ideas.md` (design constraints and a "left out" list), and individual §11 decisions that close a feature as not wanted or not now. Below is every one still in force; limits that have since been lifted are noted as lifted.

**`designs/spec/01-what-this-is.md` — the product's non-goals**
1. **The bar:** "without Final Cut's magnetic timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin ecosystem". Scopes have since been built (GR-10); the rest still stand.
2. **Multicam.**
3. **Colour grading beyond per-clip controls:** mostly lifted by grading tiers 1–4 and the HDR road map. The leftovers are listed under §11 below.
4. **Audio beyond what shipped:** no EQ, no mix buses, no Audio Units. Offline voice effects are "deferred rather than out".
5. **A plugin system:** only a graphic's JavaScript module is scriptable (G-1). R5-1 adds that effects are closed vocabularies: no user shaders and no expression language.
6. **Heavy pixel and ML work:** motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe.
7. **Any platform but macOS**, and only on Apple Silicon with macOS 26 or later.
8. **Recording:** screen recording was lifted by road map 3 and camera recording by CAM-1. Callouts (reconstructed mouse and keyboard overlays) stay out.

**`designs/spec/02-six-ideas.md` — design constraints that limit features**
9. **One kind of track:** there are no audio-only or video-only track types. This matters for buses and a track mixer.
10. **Actions, not keyframes:** there is no keyframe graph and no rubber-band automation curves.
11. **Overlap is a transition:** there is no transition track and no transition browser.
12. **"Left out":**
    - callouts and pointer effects
    - templates (partly contradicted now: G-44 ships bundled graphic templates)
    - publishing to YouTube or Vimeo
    - a stock-media library

**`designs/spec/11-decisions/` — features closed as not wanted, or held back**
13. **AVFoundation, not ffmpeg** (`foundations.md`): the product has no ffmpeg dependency. ffmpeg is only an opt-in import step that uses a copy the user installed.
14. **Codec export, CX-1:** VP9 in MP4 is not wanted, and AV1 with alpha is not wanted because no encoder supports it.
15. **Precision:**
    - PR-8: 10-bit `hevc_alpha` and 10-bit screen recording are not wanted.
    - A 16-bit APNG encoder is not wanted ("APNG is quite niche").
16. **Grading:**
    - GR-20: a wide-gamut working space for SDR projects.
    - GR-27: an Offset wheel.
    - GR-28: a qualifier on picture clips.
    - GR-29: 1,024-level scopes.
    - GR-30: a histogram behind the curves.
17. **SY-41:** no time-stretch of Frame Job's own; Keep pitch stays on Apple's time-pitch, and #299 is still open.
18. **Cloud AI** (`cloud-captions.md`): bring-your-own key only. A hosted relay (C2) is deferred; that has been your standing choice since 2026-09-30.

**Outside the spec:** `designs/adr/effects-survey.md` lists candidates you deferred on 2026-09-15. Looks, adjustment clips and LUTs were later built by grading. Still unbuilt from that list:
- flip and masks (E3)
- thirteen more filter kinds and a clock (E4)
- voice effects (E8)
- Remove Background (E9)

For the audio discussion, items 4, 9 and 10 are the ones that matter most. Professional tools put EQ and Audio Units on clips, run tracks through buses, and draw volume as rubber-band keyframes.

The audio survey is still running in the background. Once you've decided which limits go, I can rewrite §1's non-goals and record the lifts in §11.

  - **Normalize and the export target both stop near −27 LUFS.** Normalize to −1 dBFS lands there. The export's gain-only loudness target, capped at −1 dBTP, lands in the same place. Reaching −16 or −14 LUFS needs about 11–13 dB of peak reduction.

  - Clean-up applied when a voice-over lands (B8).
  - Fade curve shapes (B9).
  - Voice effects, already designed as E8 (B10).
  
  **Tier C:** beat detection, fitting music to a length, source separation, AI speech, plug-in hosting, round-trip to an audio editor, audio-type tagging, a spectrum analyzer, sample-level repair, surround.
  
  **What I could not verify:**
  - **Adobe:** helpx.adobe.com refused direct fetches (HTTP 403), so every Premiere claim comes from search-engine excerpts of the cited pages. I did not retry with a workaround.
  - **CapCut:** I found no help pages for its audio tools, so its claims rest on its marketing articles and are marked unverified. Auto Cut is the one exception, on its help site.

  - **Descript:** its per-track mono export article was linked but not read.
  - **Apple:**
    - `AUSoundIsolation`'s latency, CPU cost and quality are unmeasured, including on this file.
    - `AUAudioMix` (macOS 26) appears to need Spatial Audio remix metadata from the file, so it is probably not a general separator. Sample #12 (an iPhone Spatial Audio clip) would test this.
    - `AUPeakLimiter` does not document true-peak detection.

content.text:
I've reviewed the survey. It's at `designs/audio-survey.md`: 964 lines, cited, and untracked.

I checked its claims about Frame Job's own code, and they hold:
- The compressor sits before the volume fader, with a default threshold of −18 dB.
- The export's loudness target is a single gain, capped at −1 dBTP true peak, with no limiter.

**What your RØDE recording needs, measured on the file rather than assumed**
- **A limiter and per-clip loudness targeting:** both Normalize and the export's loudness target stop near −27 LUFS. Reaching −16 or −14 LUFS needs about 11–13 dB of peak control. Without a limiter, the export's loudness target can't reach its own number on this file.
- **A one-click "enhance voice" chain:** high-pass, then noise reduction or voice isolation, then a compressor set from the clip's own measured level, then a limiter, then the loudness target.
- **Noise floor control:** the +28.7 dB lift brings the room noise up to about −36 dBFS, and pauses are 65 % of the file. That calls for a gate or downward expander, or Apple's on-device voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`, available since macOS 13).
- **The compressor today does nothing at its defaults:** the file peaks at −18.6 dBFS, just under the −18 dB threshold.
- **Not needed first:** a high-pass alone takes only about 1 dB off the noise. The file has no clear mains hum. Its wide loudness range comes from the pauses, not uneven speech, so a dialogue leveller isn't the first need. Sibilance is unclear without a listen.

**Expected of a professional tool (tier A)**
- A true-peak limiter and per-clip loudness targeting (both above)
- EQ, de-esser and hum removal
- Voice isolation, plus a gate or expander
- A live LUFS meter, and a loudness readout per clip
- Animating pan, EQ and effect settings, with volume drawn as a line on the clip
- J- and L-cuts that keep sync, instead of the one-way Detach Audio
- Stems: each track exported as its own file
- Track faders, and processing on tracks or buses
- 24-bit audio export

**Expected by creators (tier B)**
- Ducking triggered by speech rather than clip length, using the voice model Remove Silences already runs
- De-reverb
- Hearing audio while scrubbing
- Matching one clip's tone and level to another
- Picking one channel of a stereo file (today's Mix to mono loses 6 dB when one channel is silent)
- Clean-up applied automatically when a voice-over lands
- Fade curve shapes
- Voice effects (the deferred E8)

**Nice to have (tier C):** beat detection, fitting music to a length, source separation, AI speech, plug-in hosting and surround.

**Scope:** EQ, the de-esser and hum removal lift spec §1's "no EQ". Track and bus processing lifts "mix buses". Hosting third-party plug-ins lifts "Audio Units" and the plugin non-goal. Anything built on Apple's own audio units is marked for you to rule on, since Frame Job already uses one, Apple's time-pitch, for speed-ramp audio.

**Weaker evidence:**
- **Premiere:** Adobe's help site refused direct downloads, so those claims rest on search-result excerpts of the cited pages.
- **CapCut:** it has no audio help pages, so its claims are marked unverified.
- **Resolve:** its reference manual wasn't read, so stem export, its normalization modes and where Voice Isolation sits are unconfirmed.
- **Not yet measured:** what Frame Job's existing noise reduction does to this file's noise floor. The survey names that as the first comparison, against Apple's voice isolation.

The survey also lists 13 sample recordings worth adding to `samples/`, each tied to the features it would test. Examples: a voice with air-conditioning hum, a sibilant voice, a clipped take, a laptop mic in a reverberant room, and an interview.

Should I commit the survey as it stands? Or would you rather settle the scope list first, so the survey and the new §1 can be updated together?
I think we should draft a phased plan for tier A and tier B.

A phased plan for tier A and tier B will build on the survey's gap list. I'll read that first, then check the parts of the audio pipeline the phases depend on: the processing chain, the export's gain pass, the meter, and issue #86.

result.output:
## 5. The gaps, tiered

Each gap gives what it is, who has it, why it matters here, a one-line
feasibility note on Apple Silicon and macOS 26 (AVFoundation, no ffmpeg),
and any non-goal flag. **Mic** marks what `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a` needs,
per §2's measurements.

### What the quiet desktop-mic recording needs first

The order below follows the §2 measurements, not assumptions:

| Order | Gap | Why, from §2 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A1 limiter and A2 loudness-target normalize, together | Peak normalize and the gain-only export target both stop near −27 LUFS; −16 or −14 LUFS needs 11–13 dB of peak reduction |
| 2 | B1 a voice preset chain | The compressor exists but is inert at its defaults on a −18.6 dBFS peak, because it runs before Volume |
| 3 | A5 expander, or A4 voice isolation, beside the shipped noise reduction | After the lift, the pause floor sits around −36 dBFS in 65 % of the windows |
| 4 | A3 high-pass and EQ | A standard step, though only about 1 dB here; presence and tone after that |
| Later | A6 de-esser, B3 leveller, A7 hum removal | Not indicated by the measurements: sibilance inconclusive, LRA is the pauses, no clear hum |

### Tier A: needed to be called professional-grade

**A1. A true-peak limiter, and an export loudness target that reaches its
number.** **Mic: first.**

- **What:** a lookahead, true-peak limiter on the clip strip and on the
  export's mix. The export's loudness stage limits instead of capping gain,
  so −14 LUFS means −14 LUFS.
- **Who:**
  - Resolve: the channel-strip limiter [R1], and Deliver's "Optimize
    loudness and peak" [R3].
  - FCP: Limiter and Adaptive Limiter [F4].
  - Premiere: Hard Limiter [P7], and Media Encoder's true-peak limiter
    inside loudness normalization [P9].
  - Descript: Limiter [D2].
  - ScreenFlow: peak limiting [S1].
- **Why:** quiet voice recordings have a high peak-to-loudness ratio (26 dB
  here), so gain alone hits the ceiling long before any streaming target.
- **Feasibility:** `AUPeakLimiter` exists (attack, decay, pre-gain
  −40…+40 dB) [AD3], but true-peak detection is not documented for it. A
  limiter written beside `AudioDSP.swift`'s compressor, oversampled, is the
  surer route. The mix stage belongs where the export already gains in
  float (`ExporterAudioGain.swift`). A clip limiter in the tap must carry
  the clip's gain itself, because Volume is applied after the tap. The
  preview has no post-mix insert, so a preview master limiter is an open
  design question.
- **Flags:** none named (it is dynamics, like the shipped compressor).
  **NG-AU?** if built on `AUPeakLimiter`.

**A2. Loudness-target clip normalization and level matching.** **Mic:
first.**

- **What:** "Normalize to −16 LUFS" per clip, measured over the played
  range with the BS.1770 gate, and optionally speech-only. Also "match these
  clips' loudness". A clip's measured LUFS is shown in the inspector.
- **Who:** Premiere Auto-Match, with the clip's LUFS displayed [P3]; Resolve
  clip normalization [R1] and the AI Level Matcher [R2]; Descript's LUFS
  export options [D4].
- **Why:** peak normalize lands this file at −27 LUFS while a louder take
  lands elsewhere. Loudness is what a viewer hears, and clips cut together
  need to match.
- **Feasibility:** the BS.1770-4 measurement already exists for the export
  (`Loudness.swift`, `ExporterLoudness.swift`). It needs only a per-clip
  read like Normalize's. The ×32 ceiling (AU-1) covers the gain, and A1
  catches the peaks.
- **Flags:** none named.

**A3. EQ: high-pass, low-pass, shelves and parametric bands, with voice
presets.** **Mic: fourth.**

- **Who:** every professional editor and two creator tools:
  - Resolve: a 6-band clip EQ and a track EQ with 24 dB/octave filters [R1,
    R2, R3].
  - FCP: Equalization presets, Channel EQ and Match [F1, F2, F4].
  - Premiere: Parametric Equalizer and Clarity EQ [P6, P7].
  - Descript: EQs and high-pass [D2].
  - ScreenFlow: EQ [S1].
- **Why:** desk mics pick up rumble, desk thumps and plosives, and EQ is
  the basic tone control. Several other gaps are built from it (A6, A7,
  B6).
- **Feasibility:** `AVAudioUnitEQ` offers parametric, low-pass, high-pass,
  shelf and band-stop types [AD7], and `AUNBandEQ` the same per band [AD6].
  Biquads in the tap are cheap DSP of Frame Job's own and stay live.
- **Flags:** **NG-EQ**.

**A4. ML voice isolation (speech enhancement).** **Mic: third (with A5).**

- **Who:** FCP Voice Isolation [F1]; Resolve Voice Isolation (Studio) [R2,
  R6]; Premiere Enhance Speech [P1]; Descript Studio Sound (cloud) [D1];
  Camtasia AI Noise Removal [T3]; CapCut Enhance voice (*unverified*) [C2].
- **Why:** this is now the baseline one-control fix for noisy rooms and
  cheap microphones, and the creator audience expects it. Frame Job's
  reducer handles only steady noise.
- **Feasibility:** Apple's `AUSoundIsolation` runs on the device (macOS
  13+). Its parameters are a wet/dry mix and a sound type; the
  HighQualityVoice model needs macOS 15+ [AD1]. Render it offline into
  `cache/`, as speed-ramp audio is, with a wet/dry Amount. Its latency, CPU
  cost and quality on this file are unmeasured.
- **Flags:** **NG-AU?**

**A5. Downward expander or noise gate.** **Mic: third.**

- **Who:** Resolve's expander/gate on every strip [R1]; FCP Expander,
  Noise Gate and Spectral Gate [F4].
- **Why:** gain lifts the floor (to around −36 dBFS here). An expander
  pulls the pauses down without touching the speech, and it handles
  non-steady room noise that a spectral reducer can't learn.
- **Feasibility:** `AUDynamicsProcessor` has an expansion ratio and
  threshold [AD4]. A stage written beside the compressor reuses its
  envelope follower.
- **Flags:** none named. **NG-AU?** if built on `AUDynamicsProcessor`.

**A6. De-esser.**

- **Who:** Resolve [R1]; FCP DeEsser 2 [F4]; Premiere DeEss and DeEsser
  [P5].
- **Why:** EQ presence and heavy compression, both needed for quiet voices,
  bring sibilance forward. For this file it is inconclusive (§2).
- **Feasibility:** no Apple de-esser unit was found. Either a
  side-chain-filtered compressor in `AudioDSP`, or `AUMultiBandCompressor`
  (four bands) [AD5].
- **Flags:** **NG-EQ** (a de-esser is a dynamic EQ).

**A7. Hum removal: a notch at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics.**

- **Who:** FCP Hum Removal [F1]; Premiere DeHum, DeHummer and Notch Filter
  [P5, P7]; Resolve de-hummer [R1].
- **Why:** ground-loop hum from USB and laptop chargers is common in
  desktop setups. A notch removes it surgically where a spectral reducer
  smears. Not indicated for this file (§2).
- **Feasibility:** band-stop filters at f0 and its multiples:
  `AVAudioUnitEQ`'s band-stop type [AD7], or biquads in the tap.
- **Flags:** **NG-EQ**.

**A8. Live loudness metering, and a per-clip loudness readout.**

- **Who:** Resolve loudness meters and graph [R1]; FCP MultiMeter (LUFS,
  true peak) [F5]; Premiere Loudness Meter [P8].
- **Why:** mixing to a target needs momentary, short-term and integrated
  LUFS and true peak while playing, not only after export.
- **Feasibility:** K-weighting and gating already exist (`Loudness.swift`).
  The metering build already reads every track's tap and applies the plan's
  envelope (`AudioTap.swift`, `LevelMeter.swift`).
- **Flags:** none.

**A9. Animate every audio parameter, and draw volume on the clip.**

- **What:** pan, EQ and effect parameters over time, plus a rubber-band
  volume line on the waveform.
- **Who:** Resolve automation of "virtually any control" [R1]; FCP's Audio
  Animation editor [F11]; Premiere clip and track keyframes with the Pen
  tool, and automation modes [P10, P11]; Camtasia audio points [T2].
- **Why:** a static pan or EQ per clip is a creator-tier limit. Professional
  mixes ride levels inside clips, and Frame Job's actions can't reach pan
  or effects today (audio.md).
- **Feasibility:** core and UI work with no new framework. The tap already
  schedules settings by clip span (`AudioDSPSpan`); per-parameter envelopes
  would extend that schedule.
- **Flags:** none.

**A10. Split edits (J- and L-cuts) that keep sync, and reversible
detaching.**

- **Who:** FCP Expand Audio and split edits [F10]; Premiere Unlink and
  ⌥-drag [P16].
- **Why:** J- and L-cuts are the most common dialogue edit. Frame Job's
  Detach Audio is one way, and "no control … switches a clip's audio back
  on" (audio.md).
- **Feasibility:** a model and timeline-gesture change; no framework
  needed.
- **Flags:** none.

**A11. Stems: each track, or each group of tracks, as its own file.**

- **Who:** FCP roles as separate files or a multitrack QuickTime [F9];
  Descript per-track mono files (an article title only) [D4]. Resolve and
  Premiere were not verified.
- **Why:** hand-off to a mixer, music-and-effects versions, a
  voice-without-music version for translation.
- **Feasibility:** per-track files can reuse the export with the other
  tracks silenced. A multitrack MOV would need several `AVAssetWriterInput`s
  (unverified here).
- **Flags:** **NG-ROLES** only if it is done by role rather than by track.

**A12. Track faders and track or bus processing.**

- **Who:** Resolve's mixer, buses and FlexBus [R1]; Premiere's Audio Track
  Mixer and submixes [P10]. FCP gets by without a mixer, through roles and
  compound clips [F3, F8].
- **Why:** "music 6 dB down everywhere" is one fader, not forty clip edits.
  A compressor or limiter across a whole voice track behaves differently
  from per-clip ones at clip boundaries.
- **Feasibility:** a track fader is an envelope in the plan. Track effects
  have no natural home, because composition audio tracks are not timeline
  tracks (`AudioTap.swift` notes the A/B assignment). They need a design
  spike.
- **Flags:** **NG-BUS**.

**A13. 24-bit (and float-decoded) audio export.**

- **Who:** not verified across editors.
- **Why:** a delivery and archival expectation.
- **Feasibility:** issue #86 has the design: a float decode before the gain,
  then an `audio_bits` override.
- **Flags:** none.

### Tier B: expected by the creator and screencast audience

**B1. A one-click "Enhance voice" chain.** **Mic: second.**

- **What:** high-pass → noise reduction or isolation → compressor set
  relative to the clip's measured level → limiter → loudness target. It
  writes ordinary clip settings that a person can then edit.
- **Who:** FCP Enhance Audio [F1]; Resolve AI Audio Assistant (Studio)
  [R2]; Premiere Auto Tag plus Auto-Match [P15, P3]; Descript Studio Sound
  [D1].
- **Why:** a screencaster wants one button. The shipped compressor shows
  that defaults fixed in dBFS fail on a quiet mic (§2).
- **Feasibility:** no DSP beyond A1–A5. The assistant and agents get it
  through the same tool (agent parity).
- **Flags:** inherits its parts' flags.

**B2. Speech-aware ducking.**

- **What:** keyed by voice activity, not clip extent, with a pre-roll. It
  is drawn as an envelope the person can see and edit.
- **Who:** Premiere Auto Ducking, which writes keyframes [P4]; Resolve's
  signal-keyed Ducker with lookahead [R3, R4].
- **Why:** today's ducking holds music down through every pause of a long
  voice clip (audio.md).
- **Feasibility:** the on-device voice model already runs per media for
  Remove Silences (`cleanup-tools.md`). Its speech spans can shape the duck
  envelope in the plan, deterministically, with no new framework.
- **Flags:** none.

**B3. Dialogue leveller (a slow gain rider).**

- **Who:** Resolve Dialogue Leveler [R2, R3].
- **Why:** a speaker who leans in and out, or a two-person recording. Not
  indicated for this file, whose LRA is the pauses (§2).
- **Feasibility:** computed offline from short-term loudness into the
  envelope, or a slow stage of Frame Job's own.
- **Flags:** none.

**B4. De-reverb.**

- **Who:** Premiere Reduce Reverb and DeReverb [P5, P7]; Descript Studio
  Sound "echo" [D1]; Resolve's Dialogue Separator ambience [R3].
- **Why:** laptop microphones in untreated rooms.
- **Feasibility:** no Apple de-reverb unit was found. Whether
  `AUSoundIsolation` removes reverberation is unverified.
- **Flags:** **NG-AU?** if it rides on A4.

**B5. Audio scrubbing.**

- **Who:** FCP audio skimming [F14].
- **Why:** finding a word by ear while dragging the playhead. Frame Job's
  scrub is silent (`timeline.md`).
- **Feasibility:** unverified. It needs short-grain playback at the scrub
  position.
- **Flags:** none.

**B6. Match one clip to another: EQ, level and room.**

- **Who:** FCP Match Audio [F2]; Resolve AI EQ Matcher, Level Matcher and
  Dialogue Matcher [R2].
- **Why:** a camera's scratch audio cut against the RØDE, or two sessions
  on different days.
- **Feasibility:** a spectrum difference becomes an EQ curve (needs A3). The
  level half is A2.
- **Flags:** **NG-EQ**.

**B7. Channel selection: left only, right only, dual mono.**

- **Who:** FCP channel configuration [F7]; Premiere Modify ▸ Audio Channels
  [P12]; Resolve channel mapping [R1, R4]; ScreenFlow per-channel pan and
  level [S1].
- **Why:** USB and XLR interfaces often record a mono mic onto one channel
  of a stereo file. Frame Job's Mix to mono averages the channels, which
  lands 6 dB down when one channel is silent.
- **Feasibility:** a channel pick before the mono fold in the tap. Trivial
  DSP, plus a model field.
- **Flags:** none.

**B8. Clean-up at record time.**

- **Who:** Resolve's Voiceover tool, with Voice Isolation, Dialog Leveler
  and Stereo Fixer while recording [R2]; Descript Studio Sound while
  recording [D1].
- **Why:** a voice-over should land ready to use.
- **Feasibility:** the raw file is kept, and the B1 chain is applied as

# Road map "codec-export" — AV1 and VP9 export with bundled encoders (#377)

**Opened 2026-10-27** (C0), in the worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs` on branch `codecs`, from
`75fd806`; each phase is gated and merged into main alone (CX-11). This road map's decisions are
CX-1 onwards, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`. Its brief is issue #377; the
acknowledgements its licences feed are #376.

## Goal

Frame Job exports H.264, HEVC (8-bit, 10-bit, with alpha), ProRes and still sequences, all
through AVFoundation and VideoToolbox. After this road map it also exports AV1 and VP9, encoded
by two libraries built into the app (SVT-AV1 and libvpx), into MP4 or WebM, with Opus audio in
WebM and alpha in VP9 WebM.

## The owner's choices

**2026-10-27** (the brief, `request.md`; binding; "It is super valuable to me. Bundle the
encoders."):

- **AV1 encoder: SVT-AV1 only** (pinned v4.2.0). There is no libaom.
  - Three speed choices on the export sheet: Faster = preset 8, Balanced = preset 6 (default),
    Smaller file = preset 4.
- **VP9 encoder: libvpx** (pinned v1.17.0), one speed (cpu-used 4, row-mt).
- **Export rows:** all four of these. VP9-in-MP4 is NOT wanted.
  - AV1 in MP4, with AAC audio;
  - AV1 in WebM, with Opus;
  - VP9 in WebM, with Opus;
  - VP9 + alpha in WebM.
- **WebM writer:** a Rust Matroska/WebM writer in `core/`, next to the import reader, not
  libwebm. Writing container bytes is not sample work, under the precedent of #216-R's reader.

budget; memory limits relative to physical RAM; person-only checks go in
`docs/manual-checks.md`.

4:/// The four sample-level audio effects the model carries and AVFoundation
5:/// cannot express: pan, the mono fold, the compressor and broadband noise
6:/// reduction (spec §4.2, §5.2's `AudioProps`).
7:///
8:/// **Why this file has no AVFoundation in it.** Volume, the fades and ducking
9:/// are a gain CURVE, so `audio.rs` folds them into one envelope per
10:/// composition track and `AVMutableAudioMixInputParameters` plays it back as
11:/// volume ramps. These four cannot be a curve: pan and the mono fold need
12:/// every channel at once to write to, and the compressor and the noise reducer
13:/// are functions of the samples rather than of the clock. So they are real
14:/// DSP, they run in Swift,
15:/// and they live here — plain buffers in, plain buffers out, no player, no
16:/// reader, no tap. `AudioTap.swift` is the only file that knows where the
17:/// buffers come from, which is what lets the SAME code serve the preview and
18:/// the export (§7.2's one-movie-one-description rule).
19:///
20:/// **Real-time discipline.** Everything runs inside
21:/// `MTAudioProcessingTap`'s process callback, on a thread that must not
22:/// block: every buffer these types touch is allocated once in `init` and
23:/// never grown, nothing here takes a lock, and no Swift value that could
24:/// allocate is created per sample. `frames` is never larger than the
25:/// `maxFrames` the chain was built with.
26:///
27:/// **Transparency is a property of the CALLER, not of these types.** With
28:/// pan 0, mono off, no compressor and noise reduction 0 the chain is still a
29:/// chain, and
30:/// running audio through the noise reducer's FFT round trip would change the
31:/// low bits even though it changes nothing audible. So `CompositionBuilder`
32:/// installs no tap at all on a track whose every clip is inert
33:/// (`AudioClipDSP.isInert`), and such a track's samples are the ones today's
34:/// build produces, byte for byte.

`audio.voice` is `{kind, amount, pitch −12…12}`, one per clip, with 16
kinds: voice: pitch, high, deep, robot; tone: bass, treble, bright,
telephone, radio; character: lofi, distorted; space: echo, room, hall,

and Reverb. A new `VoiceRenderer.swift` renders the clip's source WINDOW to
`cache/voiced/<digest>.caf`. The digest covers stamp, reversed, window,
kind, amount, pitch and a chain version.

reverb given mono aborts the process; an `AVAudioPlayerNode`; schedule →
`start()` → `play()`; fixed 4,096-frame calls; presets through
`auAudioUnit.currentPreset`; every parameter set and clamped; a unit removed
rather than set to wet 0; no TimePitch at 0 semitones; float CAF; per-kind
makeup gain.

Tails are cut at the clip end. `CompositionBuilder` substitutes the file per
clip, and plays DRY while a render is pending.

# Road map "audio" — a professional audio toolset (tiers A and B)

**Draft, 2026-10-30, for the owner's review. Not opened.** No phase starts until the owner has
answered "The owner's choices" below and spec §1's audio non-goals are lifted in §11. The brief
is `designs/audio-survey.md` (its tiers A and B; tier C is not in this road map). The worktree is
`.claude/worktrees/audio-updates`, branch `worktree-audio-updates`, from `33eeed0`. Decisions are
AU-2 onward, in `designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md` (AU-1, the ×32 volume ceiling, is built).

## Goal

Frame Job's audio today is a creator-tier strip: volume, fades, clip-extent ducking, pan, mono,
a compressor, steady-noise reduction, peak Normalize, and an export loudness target that only
turns the mix down (`docs/guide/audio.md`, `docs/guide/export.md`). After this road map a person
can take a quiet, noisy or uneven voice recording to a delivery loudness with one command and
then refine it: loudness they can see and target, a true-peak limiter, EQ, a gate, a de-esser,
hum removal, voice isolation, parameters that move over time, J- and L-cuts, track faders and
buses, stems, speech-aware ducking, matching, scrubbing and voice effects. Every control has its
MCP mirror, as every control does today.

## What it delivers first

The owner's recording, `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a`, peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated
loudness of −44.7 LUFS. Peak Normalize and the export's loudness target both stop near −27 LUFS
(the survey's §2), because neither can reduce a peak. **After AP2, one Normalize press in
Loudness mode takes it to the chosen target (−16 LUFS by default) at −1 dBTP.** After AP6, one
Enhance Voice press also cleans it: the high-pass, the noise floor in the pauses (about
−36 dBFS once lifted, 65 % of the file), the compressor set from the clip's own level, the
limiter and the target.

## The owner's choices (needed before AP0)

Each has a recommendation; the owner's answer is recorded as an AU- decision before any code.

1. **Scope (spec §1).** Lift "no EQ" and "no mix buses", and allow Apple's own audio units
   inside Frame Job (as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for speed-ramp audio). Hosting
   third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out of this road map (tier C, C5). *Recommended.*
2. **Normalize's default.** Keep peak normalize as the button's default until AP2's limiter
   lands, then make **Loudness** the default with Peak a choice beside it. *Recommended.*
3. **The default loudness target.** −16 LUFS integrated at −1 dBTP (voice platforms and
   podcasts), with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128) as quick picks.
   *Recommended.*
4. **Own DSP or Apple's units for the live stages.** Frame Job's own DSP for EQ, gate,
   de-esser, hum notch and limiter, written beside the compressor: live in the tap,
   deterministic, testable against analytic responses. Apple's units only where Frame Job cannot
   write its own: ML voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`) and E8's voice effects, both rendered
   offline as speed-ramp audio is. AP0's spike S1 confirms or overturns this. *Recommended.*
5. **One fixed chain order, not a user-ordered list.** Channels → high-pass and EQ → hum notch
   → isolation or noise reduction → gate → de-esser → compressor → limiter, each stage off by
   default and inert when off. A closed vocabulary like every other effect (§11 R5-1), and the
   order an engineer would choose for voice. *Recommended.*

Asked later, at the phase that needs them (each has a recommendation there): how the volume
line is edited (AP8), the split-edit model (AP9), track processing in the preview and the stem
format (AP10), and where speech spans live for ducking (AP11).

## The orchestrator's defaults (each one the owner can change)

- **Working arrangement:** this worktree; each phase built through litecode, gated, committed
  and merged into main alone, as codec-export (CX-11) and grading (GR-25) did.
- **Agent parity:** every new property is a `set_audio` key, every new command a tool, every
  new answer readable through `get_project`.
- **Proof currency:** exports decoded to PCM and measured by the proof's own arithmetic
  (`phase5_proof.py`'s BS.1770 and 4× true-peak oversampler), synthetic fixtures with known
  answers, and the owner's samples where present. What only ears can judge is a row in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`.
- **Samples:** the owner records the survey's §6 list. A phase uses a sample when it exists and
  a synthetic fixture otherwise; no phase waits for one.
- **Persisted fields** carry serde defaults and bump the format (`core/CLAUDE.md`); an older
  project opens unchanged and sounds the same.

## How it fits the tree (at `33eeed0`)

- **The clip strip runs in a tap, before the fader.** `AudioTap.swift` (595) puts one
  `MTAudioProcessingTap` (PreEffects) on each composition audio track and schedules each clip's
  settings by span (`AudioDSPSpan`). `AudioDSP.swift` (**890, over the cap**) holds pan, the mono
  fold, the compressor (default threshold −18 dB) and noise reduction, real-time safe. Volume,
  fades and ducking come after the tap, as the core's envelope played as volume ramps
  (`core/src/audio.rs` 537, `audio_duck.rs` 136). **A new live stage sees the clip at its
  recorded level**, so a level-relative stage (limiter, gate) must be told the clip's gain.
- **The preview has no post-mix insert; the export does.** One tap per input, already used by
  the meter (`LevelMeter.swift` 400, which sums per-track peaks as an upper bound, not the mix).
  The export measures a 32-bit float mix and gains it in `ExporterAudioGain.swift` (179); its
  write pass still decodes 16-bit integers (#86).
- **Offline renders have a pattern.** Speed-ramp audio renders into `cache/ramp-audio/` through
  `RampAudioRenders` (a serial queue, owners, a wait in the export, dry while pending).
- **Loudness exists once.** `Loudness.swift` (**674, over the cap**) is BS.1770-4 for the
  export; `ExporterLoudness.swift` (211) its measurement pass.
- **The model.** `AudioProps` lives in `core/src/model_props.rs` (551), checked by
  `props_check.rs` (526) and clamped by `actions_clamp.rs` (386); pan, mono, compressor, noise
  reduction, duck and keep pitch are BASE-only (`InspectorBinding+Writes.swift`'s
  `structural(audio:)`), and only volume, mute and the fades animate.
- **Caches.** Peaks, sync features and speech (Silero VAD) per media, on the cache lane
  (`MediaCacheLane.swift`); a loudness cache would be a fifth beside them.

## Phases

| Phase | Survey items | What a person gets |
|---|---|---|
| AP0 | — | Scope lifted, the spike's answers, the files split |
| AP1 | A2, A8 (readout) | A clip's LUFS shown; Normalize to a loudness |
| AP2 | A1, A13 | A true-peak limiter; the export reaches its loudness; 24-bit |
| AP3 | A3, A7, B7 | EQ and high-pass, hum removal, channel selection |
| AP4 | A5, A6 | Gate/expander, de-esser |
| AP5 | A4, B4 | Voice isolation; de-reverb if isolation does it |
| AP6 | B1, B3, B8 | Enhance Voice; the leveller; clean-up when a voice-over lands |
| AP7 | A8 | Live LUFS and true-peak meter |
| AP8 | A9 | Every audio parameter animates; the volume line on the clip |
| AP9 | A10 | J- and L-cuts that keep sync; reversible Detach |
| AP10 | A12, A11 | Track faders, track and master processing, stems |
| AP11 | B2, B9 | Ducking by speech; fade and crossfade shapes |
| AP12 | B6 | Match one clip's level and tone to another |
| AP13 | B5 | Audio while scrubbing |
| AP14 | B10 | Voice effects (E8, #123) |

AP1–AP6 are the voice block, in the order the owner's recording needs them. AP7 onward is the
mixing block and can be reordered freely; only AP12 needs AP3, and AP6 needs AP2–AP5.

### AP0 — scope, the record, the tolls and the spike

- **Decisions:** AU-2 (the scope, from choice 1), AU-3 (the chain, choices 4 and 5), AU-4 (the
  loudness defaults, choices 2 and 3). Spec §1's non-goal sentence rewritten; this road map
  opened.
- **Tolls, each a pure move landed and gated alone:** `AudioDSP.swift` cut at its MARKs (the
  compressor and noise reduction into their own files, the chain kept); `AudioTap.swift`'s
  schedule and parameters (its first two MARKs) out of the tap; `Loudness.swift` cut below the
  cap; `AudioProps` and its vocabulary out of `model_props.rs` into a new `model_audio.rs`.
- **Spike S, its rule fixed before its run, its record here:**
  - **S1 — own DSP or Apple units, live.** A biquad EQ and Frame Job's limiter against
    `AVAudioUnitEQ`, `AUNBandEQ` and `AUPeakLimiter` driven inside the tap: byte-identical
    exports run twice, preview against export, CPU per track at eight stages, latency.
  - **S2 — voice isolation.** `AUSoundIsolation` rendered offline over the owner's recording:
    speed against real time, latency, determinism across runs, the pause floor and the speech
    band against the shipped noise reducer, and whether it reduces reverberation (B4's
    question), on a reverberant sample if one exists.
  - **S3 — tracks and the master in the preview.** Whether one composition audio track ever
    carries two timeline tracks; the error of a track chain run per composition track during an
    overlap (zero for linear stages, measured for dynamics); the options for a preview master
    limiter (none and say so, per-track, or an offline premix); rebuilding the true mix from the
    taps for a LUFS meter.
  - **S4 — a loudness cache.** K-weighted 100 ms block energies per media: size, build time on
    a 20-minute file, and integrated LUFS over any window against `Loudness.swift` measuring an
    export of the same window (agreement within 0.1 LU).
- **Acceptance:** `make gate` after each toll; the spike's verdicts recorded here.

### AP1 — loudness you can see and target (A2, A8's readout)

- A per-media loudness cache (`cache/loudness/<id>.bin`, S4's format) on the cache lane after
  peaks, current by `CacheStamp` like the others.
- The Volume section reads the clip's integrated loudness (gated, over the window that plays)
  and its true peak beside the Gain row.
- Normalize gains a **Loudness** mode: a target in LUFS, each clip of a selection to the same
  target, which is what "match these clips" means. Until AP2, a clip whose peak would pass the
  ceiling stops short and says where it landed, as the volume ceiling does today.
  `normalize_clip` gains `mode` and `target_lufs`.
- **Proof:** exports of normalised fixtures measured by the proof's BS.1770 within ±0.5 LU;
  the owner's recording; a selection of two levels landing equal.

### AP2 — limiters, and an export that reaches its loudness (A1, A13)

- A **clip limiter** stage in the tap: lookahead, 4× oversampled true-peak detection, a ceiling
  in dBTP. Because the fader is downstream, the stage is told the clip's gain (decision AU-n:
  the base volume, with fades and ducks only ever lowering it), and its lookahead is a lead
  like noise reduction's (SY-25).
- The **export:** a float decode before the gain (#86, closing it), a master limiter in the
  float write pass so the loudness target limits instead of capping, and an `audio_bits` choice
  of 16 or 24 on WAV and AIFF.
- Loudness Normalize uses the clip limiter, so the owner's recording reaches −16 LUFS at
  −1 dBTP. If choice 2 says so, Loudness becomes the button's default here.
- **Proof:** every export's true peak at or under its ceiling by the proof's oversampler; the
  loudness target met within ±0.5 LU on `phase5_proof.py`'s crest fixture, which today lands
  quieter; a 24-bit file decoded with its low bits used; the owner's recording.
- **Manual check:** no pumping or distortion on speech and on music.

### AP3 — EQ, hum removal and channel selection (A3, A7, B7)

- **EQ:** a high-pass with a slope, a low-pass, low and high shelves and a number of parametric
  bands (set at AP3), with voice presets (rumble cut, de-mud, presence). An EQ section in the
  Sound sub-tab with the response curve drawn.
- **Hum:** notches at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, depth and harmonic count.
- **Channels:** both, left only, right only, swapped, before the mono fold, so a mic recorded
  on one channel of a stereo file plays at its level.
- **Model:** `audio.eq`, `audio.hum`, `audio.channels`; format bump; MCP keys.
- **Proof:** tones and sweeps through each band against the biquad's analytic response
  (±0.1 dB); notch depth at each harmonic; a channel pick sample-identical to its source channel.

### AP4 — gate, expander and de-esser (A5, A6)

- A downward **expander/gate** sharing the compressor's envelope follower: threshold relative
  to the clip's measured level (AP1), ratio, range, attack, hold, release.
- A **de-esser:** a compressor keyed on a high band (frequency, threshold, range).
- **Model, inspector, MCP** as AP3; format bump.
- **Proof:** a tone burst over noise, the pause floor lowered by the range and the burst
  untouched; sibilant noise bursts reduced in band and the voice band untouched; the owner's
  recording's pause floor.

### AP5 — voice isolation (A4; B4's verdict)

- **Isolation** by `AUSoundIsolation` (S2), rendered offline per clip window into
  `cache/isolated/` on the ramp-audio pattern: an Amount (wet/dry), dry while pending, the
  export waiting for its render, re-rendered when the window or the file changes.
- **De-reverb (B4):** if S2 measured reverberation removed, it is this control and the guide
  says so; otherwise B4 is filed with tier C and the measurement.
- **Proof:** the render aligned with the dry clip within a sample (cross-correlation); the pause
  floor and the speech band against the dry clip; dry while pending; an export that waits.
- **Manual check:** artefacts on the owner's voice at Amount 100 % and 50 %.

### AP6 — Enhance Voice, the leveller, and clean-up when a voice-over lands (B1, B3, B8)

- **Enhance Voice** (Clip menu, a button in the Sound sub-tab, an `enhance_voice` tool): reads
  the clip's loudness, its peak and the noise floor over the VAD cache's non-speech spans, then
  writes ORDINARY settings a person can see and change — high-pass, isolation or noise
  reduction, gate, de-esser if the high band is hot, a compressor set from the clip's own
  level, the limiter and the loudness target. One undo step; pressing it twice changes nothing.
- **Leveller (B3):** a slow gain-rider stage for a speaker who moves on and off the mic, off by
  default, turned on by Enhance Voice when the speech's short-term loudness range calls for it.
- **At record time (B8):** a recorder setting, "Enhance the microphone when it lands", applying
  Enhance Voice to the Microphone clip in the landing's grouped edit.
- **Proof:** the owner's recording to −16 LUFS ±0.5 at −1 dBTP with its pause floor lowered;
  idempotence; one undo step; a voice-over that lands enhanced.

### AP7 — live loudness and true-peak metering (A8)

- Momentary, short-term and integrated LUFS and true peak while playing, over the true mix
  (S3's method), with a reset; the per-clip readout is AP1's.
- **Proof:** a probe compiled from `app/Sources` fed EBU Tech 3341's test signals, each within
  its tolerance.

### AP8 — every audio parameter animates; the volume line (A9)

- Pan, EQ gains and frequencies, gate, de-esser, compressor and limiter settings, isolation's
  Amount and the leveller's target as action ends; the tap's schedule carries per-parameter
  ramps from the core, not one constant per span. Switches (a stage on or off) still change at
  an action's end, as booleans do (§5.4).
- **The volume line:** each clip draws its envelope over its waveform; dragging it edits the
  level. **Asked at AP8:** edit through actions (a point is an action's end, which keeps §2's
  "Actions, not keyframes"; recommended) or add keyframes (lifting it).
- **Proof:** exports of an animated pan and EQ against analytic gains; the line drawn where
  the plan's ramps are.

### AP9 — split edits (A10)

- J- and L-cuts that keep sync, and Detach Audio made reversible (Attach Audio).
- **Asked at AP9:** a LINKED pair — Detach's two clips carrying one link id, moved, cut and
  deleted together, with ⌥-drag trimming one half alone (recommended: it fits one kind of
  track, and an audio lead on its own track cannot collide with "overlap is a transition") —
  or one clip whose audio window extends past its picture.
- **Proof:** core tests of every edit on a linked pair; exports with the audio leading and
  trailing the picture by a known amount.

### AP10 — tracks, buses and stems (A12, A11)

- A **track fader and pan** in the header and the Track menu (an envelope term in the core, as
  a track's mute is).
- **Track and master processing** by S3's verdict, asked at AP10: the master limiter in the
  export at least; in the preview, as S3 found possible, or said plainly where it differs.
- **Stems:** each track, or a chosen set, as its own file in one export; **asked at AP10:**
  separate files (recommended) or a multitrack movie if S3 measured it to work.
- **Proof:** fader arithmetic on an export; the stems summed against the full mix (a null within
  quantisation when no master dynamics run).

### AP11 — ducking by speech, and fade shapes (B2, B9)

- **Ducking by speech:** the ducking clip's speech spans from the VAD cache, with pre-roll, hold
  and release, drawn as the envelope it makes. **Asked at AP11:** spans persisted on the media
  (a detected field, as Camera Log's is; recommended, so the plan stays a function of the
  project) or handed to the plan by the host.
- **Fade and crossfade shapes:** linear, S-curve, +3 dB and −3 dB, sampled by the core like an
  eased action.
- **Proof:** the plan's ramps against fixture spans; exports of each fade shape against its
  formula.

### AP12 — match one clip to another (B6)

- **Match Loudness** to a reference clip (AP1's measurement) and **Match EQ:** the reference's
  and the target's average speech spectra fitted to AP3's bands. A command and a tool.
- **Proof:** pink noise tilted by a known EQ matched back within ±1 dB a band.

### AP13 — audio while scrubbing (B5)

- Short grains of the mix at the scrub position while the playhead is dragged, off when the
  drag stops; the design is set at AP13 against what AVFoundation allows.
- **Proof:** a probe of the grain scheduler. **Manual check:** the feel, and no clicks.

### AP14 — voice effects (B10, E8)

- E8 as designed and measured (`designs/adr/effects-survey.md`, #123): sixteen kinds as fixed
  chains of Apple units rendered offline, with an amount and a pitch. Closes #123.

### Closing the road map

The ADR in `designs/adr/audio.md`, this file and the survey archived with their rows in
`archive/INDEX.md`, the guide pages and README highlights, and every unfinished item filed as an
issue.

## Risks

- **CPU in the live tap.** Up to eight stages per clip on every composition track, real-time.
  S1 measures it; a stage that cannot run live renders offline as isolation does.
- **Preview against export.** Master processing may exist only in the export (S3). If so, the
  guide and the meter say so rather than leave the two to differ silently.
- **Offline renders.** Isolation and voice effects add render time and cache space; both reuse
  the ramp-audio queue's owners, waits and pruning.
- **ML determinism.** If `AUSoundIsolation` is not byte-repeatable, its proofs measure levels
  and alignment, not bytes.
- **Format bumps.** AP3, AP4, AP8, AP9, AP10 and AP11 each add persisted fields; each bump has
  its `schema_vN.rs` test.
- **File caps.** Five audio files are at or over 600 lines today; AP0's tolls come first, and
  each later phase budgets its own.

## Not in this road map

Tier C (beat detection, retiming music, source separation, AI speech, third-party plug-in
hosting, round-trips to an audio editor, automatic tagging, a spectrum analyser, sample-level
repair, surround) and anything the owner's answers move out.

I've drafted the plan in `designs/audio.md` (315 lines). It has 15 phases, AP0 to AP14, covering tiers A and B; the "AP" prefix keeps phase numbers apart from the AU- decision numbers. The phases come in two blocks: the voice work first, because that's what your RØDE recording needs, then the mixing work, which can be reordered freely. Nothing starts until you answer five questions (below).

| Phase | What you get |
|---|---|
| AP0 | Scope lifted in the spec. A technical spike: Apple's built-in effects versus our own code, Apple's voice isolation tested on your file, how track effects could work during playback, and a loudness cache. The audio files over the 600-line cap get split first. |
| AP1 | Each clip's loudness (LUFS) shown in the inspector; Normalize can target a loudness |
| **AP2** | **A true-peak limiter; the export's loudness target finally reaches its number; 24-bit export (#86)** |
| AP3 | EQ and high-pass, hum removal, picking one channel of a stereo file |
| AP4 | Gate/expander, de-esser |
| AP5 | Voice isolation, using Apple's on-device model; de-reverb only if isolation turns out to do it |
| AP6 | One-click Enhance Voice, a leveller, and clean-up applied as a voice-over lands |
| AP7 | Live loudness and true-peak meter |
| AP8 | Every audio setting can change over time; a volume line drawn on each clip |
| AP9 | J- and L-cuts that keep sync; Detach Audio becomes reversible |
| AP10 | Track faders, track and master processing, stems |
| AP11 | Ducking triggered by speech; fade curve shapes |
| AP12 | Match one clip's loudness and tone to another |
| AP13 | Hearing audio while scrubbing |
| AP14 | Voice effects (the already-designed E8, #123) |

**Your recording:** after AP2, one Normalize press in Loudness mode takes it to −16 LUFS at −1 dBTP. After AP6, Enhance Voice also cleans it up: high-pass, the noise in the pauses, a compressor set from the clip's own level, and the limiter.

**Choices needed before AP0** (each has a recommendation in the plan):
1. **Scope:** lift spec §1's "no EQ" and "no mix buses", and allow Apple's built-in audio effects. Hosting third-party plug-ins stays out of this plan.
2. **Normalize's default:** stays Peak until the AP2 limiter exists, then becomes Loudness.
3. **Loudness target:** −16 LUFS by default, with −14 (YouTube) and −23 (broadcast) one click away.
